$schemaNote: Windows software -> Linux outcome. Used by `switchcheck linux`. First matching entry wins; keep specific entries above generic ones. kind: native | alternative | wine | proton | blocked.

apps.name: Chrome Remote Desktop
apps.note: No Linux host support; use RustDesk (self-hostable) or Sunshine+Moonlight instead.

apps.name: Microsoft Edge
apps.note: Microsoft stopped updating the Linux desktop build; switch to Chromium/Chrome/Brave.

apps.name: Firefox
apps.note: Ships with most distros; Flatpak available.

apps.name: WeChat
apps.note: Official native Linux client since WeChat 4.0 (wechat-beta on flathub/deb).

apps.name: QQ Music
apps.note: No official Linux client; use the web player or a third-party client.

apps.name: WeCom (企业微信)
apps.note: No official Linux client; web version covers most features, or run under Wine/Bottles.

apps.name: Microsoft Teams
apps.note: Microsoft ships a PWA only; install it from Edge/Chrome or use the web app.

apps.name: Skype
apps.note: Skype is being retired; web client still works.

apps.name: WhatsApp
apps.note: No official desktop client; use the web app (WhatsApp Web).

apps.name: LibreOffice
apps.note: Native; default office suite on most distros.

apps.name: Microsoft Office
apps.note: No native Linux build. Office web (free) covers most needs; OnlyOffice is the closest offline suite with strong .docx fidelity.

apps.name: Microsoft Outlook
apps.note: Use Outlook web, or Thunderbird/Evolution for accounts.

apps.name: Adobe Acrobat
apps.note: No Linux version; every distro ships capable PDF readers.
apps.alt: Okular, Firefox PDF, Master PDF Editor

apps.name: Adobe Photoshop
apps.note: No native version. Photoshop CC up to ~2021 runs under Wine/Bottles; for a native workflow use GIMP (+ G'MIC) or Photopea (browser, nearly 1:1 with PS shortcuts).

apps.name: Adobe Creative Cloud app
apps.note: The CC desktop app does not run on Linux; individual apps vary (see Photoshop/Premiere entries).

apps.name: AutoCAD
apps.note: No Linux version; web viewer exists.

apps.name: Blender
apps.note: Official Linux builds; one of the best-cared-for Linux apps anywhere.

apps.name: VS Code
apps.note: Official .deb/.rpm; VSCodium if you want it without Microsoft telemetry.

apps.name: Visual Studio (IDE)
apps.note: The full IDE is Windows-only; .NET/C# development works well on Linux with Rider (free for non-commercial) or VS Code + C# Dev Kit.
apps.alt: JetBrains Rider, VS Code + C# Dev Kit

apps.name: JetBrains IDE / Android Studio
apps.note: Official Linux builds; Android Studio ships Linux natively too.

apps.name: Notion
apps.note: No official client; web or community wrappers.

apps.name: AutoHotkey
apps.note: AHK itself has no official Linux build; scripts need rewriting.

apps.name: Snipaste
apps.note: A Linux beta exists but lags; Flameshot is the standard.

apps.name: 7-Zip
apps.note: Official Linux build since 21.x; p7zip in every repo.

apps.name: Total Commander
apps.alt: Krusader, Double Commander (very close), Midnight Commander

apps.name: Xshell / XFTP
apps.alt: WindTerm, Tabby, WezTerm; sftp:// in file managers

apps.name: WinSCP
apps.note: Windows-only; most of its uses map to native tools.

apps.name: PuTTY
apps.note: In every distro repo (though a real terminal + ssh is nicer).

apps.name: Postman
apps.note: Official Linux builds; consider Hoppscotch (web) as a lighter alt.

apps.name: Internet Download Manager
apps.alt: Motrix, Persepolis, uGet + aria2, or browser downloads

apps.name: Thunder (迅雷)
apps.note: No official Linux client; runs under Wine with quirks.

apps.name: Baidu Netdisk (百度网盘)
apps.note: Official Linux client (deb/rpm) exists; verify it still matches Windows features.

apps.name: OneDrive
apps.note: No official Linux client; the abraunegg onedrive client is mature and scriptable.

apps.name: Dropbox
apps.note: Official Linux client (proprietary filesystem extension needs matching packages).

apps.name: Google Drive
apps.note: No official sync client; mount via rclone or GNOME Online Accounts.

apps.name: Git
apps.note: Native; add GitButler/GitHub CLI for the GUI/CLI bits you miss.

apps.name: Godot Engine
apps.note: Official Linux builds; the engine's home platform.

apps.name: Android SDK tools
apps.note: The SDK is Java-based and runs natively; adb/fastboot/emulator all work on Linux.

apps.name: Clash-family proxy GUI
apps.note: Clash Verge Rev / FlClash ship official Linux builds.

apps.name: Unreal Engine
apps.note: Epic ships Linux binaries for UE (via Epic account); launcher itself needs Heroic/Lutris.

apps.name: Docker Desktop
apps.note: Docker Desktop for Linux exists; plain Docker Engine + Compose is lighter.

apps.name: VMware Workstation
apps.note: Official Linux build; free for personal use since 2024 (Broadcom account required).

apps.name: VirtualBox
apps.note: Official Linux builds; or use GNOME Boxes/virt-manager for QEMU/KVM.

apps.name: WSL
apps.note: You will not need WSL on Linux — it IS Linux. Distros import via LXC/systemd-nspawn if needed.

apps.name: Node.js
apps.note: Native; use nvm/fnm or distro packages.

apps.name: Java
apps.note: OpenJDK in every distro repo; Temurin has official builds.

apps.name: .NET SDK
apps.note: Official Linux builds (modern .NET); .NET Framework (4.x) apps need Wine.

apps.name: PotPlayer
apps.note: Windows-only; the Linux default experience is arguably better.

apps.name: foobar2000
apps.alt: DeaDBeeF (very close), Audacious, Strawbery Music Player

apps.name: NetEase Cloud Music (网易云音乐)
apps.note: The official Linux client lags/discontinued; a rich web player and community clients cover it.

apps.name: iTunes / Apple Music
apps.note: No Linux client; Apple Music web works.

apps.name: Sogou Pinyin (搜狗输入法)
apps.note: Sogou has an official Linux IME (fcitx-based); plain fcitx5+pinyin is excellent without it.

apps.name: Epic Games Store
apps.note: No official client; Heroic Games Launcher runs EGS games (incl. free claims) natively via Wine/Proton.

apps.name: Battle.net
apps.note: Runs well under Bottles/Lutris; Blizzard games vary ( WoW/D4 playable, competitive titles risky).

apps.name: GOG Galaxy
apps.note: No official client; Heroic covers GOG libraries natively.

apps.name: Ubisoft Connect
apps.note: Runs via Lutris/Bottles; game outcomes vary.

apps.name: Steam
apps.note: Official Linux client; Proton runs most of the catalog (see the games section of this report).

apps.name: Roblox
apps.note: No official support and the anti-cheat blocks Wine; Sober (Android-runtime port) is the working community path.

apps.name: Minecraft
apps.note: Official Linux launcher; Prism Launcher is the community favorite (mods/instances).

apps.name: Genshin Impact (原神)
apps.note: No official Linux client; community launchers (an-anime-bazaar team) keep it playable — check the current anti-cheat climate before spending money.

apps.name: Honkai: Star Rail
apps.note: Community launcher path; same caveats as Genshin.

apps.name: NetEase Minecraft (我的世界中国版)
apps.alt: Prism Launcher + 正版 Java 版

apps.name: 360 suite
apps.note: Windows-specific security/optimizer tools; not needed and not available. Linux needs no antivirus for desktop use.
apps.alt: nothing — UWP: apt/flatpak keep apps updated

apps.name: Huorong (火绒安全)
apps.alt: clamav only if you need scanning

apps.name: Third-party antivirus
apps.note: Not available and not needed on a Linux desktop.
apps.alt: built-in hygiene, clamav for file scanning

apps.name: Driver updater tools
apps.note: Drivers ship with the kernel; vendor tools are Windows-only.

apps.name: GeForce Experience / NVIDIA App
apps.note: No Linux equivalent app, but driver updates come from the distro; use nvidia-settings for the rest.

apps.name: Rufus
apps.note: You will use it to make the Linux USB itself; on Linux, use dd/Etcher/Ventoy.

apps.name: VDI client
apps.note: Both ship Linux clients; verify your company's portal version.

apps.name: CAJViewer (知网)
apps.note: Windows-only; CNKI web reader covers most needs.

apps.name: Tax / invoicing software (税务/开票)
apps.note: China tax-control plugins are Windows/IE-specific — this is the #1 hard blocker for business machines in China. Keep a Windows VM or dual-boot for tax season.
apps.alt: VM with Windows, or a second machine

apps.name: Banking security control (网银控件/U盾)
apps.note: USB-key drivers and ActiveX controls are Windows-only; mobile banking apps usually cover transfers.
apps.alt: bank's mobile app, or Windows VM

default.note: Not in SwitchCheck's knowledge base yet — search the distro repos, Flathub, and the web for a Linux version or equivalent.
